lines.text: Earth's field is very close to a bar magnet. Two things about it are not obvious.
The second one is the whole story here.
The best-fit dipole sits 610 kilometres from Earth's centre.
A tenth of an Earth radius. Small enough that you can barely see it here.
Field strength falls off with distance from the dipole — not from the Earth.
So a surface of equal field strength rides off centre with the dipole.
On one side that surface is fifteen hundred kilometres up. On the other, three hundred.
The gap between them is twice the offset. That is the whole anomaly.
Now fly something at five hundred kilometres.
For most of the orbit it flies under that surface. Over one region it is above it.
That region is the antipode of the offset — and it is over Brazil.
